Expectation1: Help out during difficult times or emergencies.
Situation1: You get a frantic call from your friend whose car has broken down on the side of the highway late at night, and they need you to come get them immediately.
Expectation2: Participate in project planning and provide accurate time estimates
Situation2: The planning session is informal, and the timeline can still shift without major impact
Story: My phone buzzed just as I was reviewing the project specs for tomorrow’s planning session. It was Sam, my oldest friend, his voice shaky. “My car died on the highway. Can you come get me? Please?” I glanced at the clock—11:30 p.m. I knew he wouldn’t call unless it was serious. As a friend, I felt a surge of responsibility; he’d do the same for me. But as an engineer, I was already behind on my prep for the planning meeting. My team was counting on me to provide accurate time estimates, and I’d promised myself I’d finally get ahead tonight. The session was informal, sure, and the timeline wasn’t set in stone, but I hated letting my team down. My mind raced, torn between the urgency in Sam’s voice and the silent weight of my professional commitment. I stared at my keys, heart pounding, caught between two worlds that both needed me right now.
